newsitem.title: UK: France to step up hunt for Caroline's killer.
newsitem.headline: France to step up hunt for Caroline's killer.

text.p: French authorities will redouble their efforts to find the killer of British teenager Caroline Dickinson, Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine said on Wednesday.
Vedrine was responding to a request by British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook to provide more information for the girl's family and to examine whether investigators had sufficient resources.
Caroline was on a school trip to Brittany, western France, when she was raped and strangled while other girls slept in her youth hostel dormitory in Pleine-Fougeres on July 18, 1996.
"The French government can continue to do what it has been doing up to now -- but with added intensity," Vedrine told reporters after talks in London with Cook.
Caroline's family wants investigating magistrate Gerard Zaug taken off the case, but Vedrine said it was not fair to criticise the efforts that have gone into the probe.
"But we completely understand and share the strong feelings that the case has raised in Britain and we won't be satisfied until a solution has been found," he said.
Cook welcomed the assurance that France would respond to the government's requests as a matter of urgency.
Police arrested a homeless local man a few days after Caroline's murder but released him after he retracted a confession made under interrogation and DNA tests cleared him.
The girl's family is pressing for wider genetic testing.
